module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Sum of two squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5

Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ where $a, b, c, d$ are
nonnegative integers.

Zhi-Wei Sun has offered a \$3,500 prize for the first proof.

*References:*
- [A303656](https://oeis.org/A303656)
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of four squares," arXiv preprint:
  https://arxiv.org/abs/1701.05868v10
- Z.-W. Sun, "Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem," Journal of Number Theory:
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf
- Z.-W. Sun, "Restricted sums of three or four squares":
  http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/Square-sum.pdf
- Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations:
  https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA303656

/-- The predicate that `n` can be written as $a^2 + b^2 + 3^c + 5^d$ for nonnegative integers. -/
def A (n : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b c d : ℕ, n = a ^ 2 + b ^ 2 + 3 ^ c + 5 ^ d

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : A 2 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : A 3 :=
  ⟨1, 0, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : A 4 :=
  ⟨1, 1, 0, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_5 : A 5 :=
  ⟨0, 1, 1, 0, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_6 : A 6 :=
  ⟨0, 0, 0, 1, by norm_num⟩

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_25 : A 25 :=
  ⟨1, 4, 1, 1, by norm_num⟩

/--
**Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture (A303656)**: Any integer $n > 1$ can be written as the sum of two
squares, a power of 3, and a power of 5.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 < n) : A n := by
  sorry

end OeisA303656

findings.description: The final reference is labeled “Zhi-Wei Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture and variations,” but its AIMS PDF URL opens an unrelated paper on quadratic residues. This is a bibliographic error only; the mathematical conjecture is correctly supported by the OEIS entry and arXiv:1701.05868v10.
findings.source_evidence: The linked PDF, https://www.aimspress.com/aimspress-data/era/2020/2/PDF/1935-9179_2020_2_589.pdf, is Fedor Petrov and Zhi-Wei Sun, “Proof of some conjectures involving quadratic residues,” Electronic Research Archive 28(2) (2020), 589–597, DOI 10.3934/era.2020031. Its title, abstract, and references concern quadratic residues, not the 1-3-5 conjecture.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove this unrelated reference or replace its URL with the intended source about the 1-3-5 conjecture. Retain arXiv:1701.05868v10, Conjecture 4.1(i), as the direct reference for the formalized claim.

findings.description: The bibliography describes “Refining Lagrange's four-square theorem” as a Journal of Number Theory article, but the accompanying RefineFourSquareTh.pdf URL points to lecture slides rather than that article.
findings.source_evidence: http://maths.nju.edu.cn/~zwsun/RefineFourSquareTh.pdf is a 50-slide talk dated December 2, 2016; its final slide separately references the paper arXiv:1604.06723. The abstract page https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06723 identifies the article as J. Number Theory 175 (2017), 167–190.
findings.suggested_fix: Either describe the linked document as Sun's 2016 lecture slides, or replace the URL with https://arxiv.org/abs/1604.06723 or https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jnt.2016.11.008 for the cited journal article.

reformulations.difference: OEIS phrases the conjecture as positivity of a representation count normalized by a ≤ b. Lean instead asserts existence through A, with no ordering constraint on the two square roots.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A positive count is equivalent to existence of an ordered representation. Any witnesses for A can be ordered by swapping a and b, preserving a²+b²; conversely, ordered witnesses satisfy A immediately. The scratch file proves both the pointwise equivalence and its universally quantified version. It also proves equivalence with the paper's set equality: every represented number is at least 2 because 3^c and 5^d are each at least 1.

sources_consulted: OEIS A303656, revision #44 dated May 30, 2026, including definition, comments, examples, and displayed terms; read through https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A303/A303656.seq because direct OEIS requests returned HTTP 403.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1701.05868v10 — definition of ℕ, Conjecture 4.1 and Remark 4.1, and bibliography.
review.notes: No mathematical misformalizations were found in A, the six test theorems, or conjecture. The OEIS entry still records the claim as a conjecture, consistent with research open. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, Lean checked the ordered/unordered, set-equality, and integer/natural reformulations without using the sorry-backed conjecture. Boundary proofs establish ¬ A 0 and ¬ A 1; all six existing tests are sorry-free. Computation found representations for every n from 2 through 200 and reproduced all 90 displayed OEIS counts. All experiments were confined to /workspace/review; pre-existing harness changes in lakefile.toml and run/ were left untouched.
